transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-10
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Marta Li (Spectral), Jonah Meyer (Spectral), Priya Narang (Spectral), Ethan Ross (Spectral)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking endpoints and how to integrate with Spectral's vector store. Covered candidate generation, reorder/rerank endpoint, Console traces, Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, and security questions (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: pilot pricing and POC kickoff.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings and reranker endpoints
- Vector DB integration and candidate generation
- Tradeoffs: latency vs cost, hosted vs dedicated
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Demo of Console tracing and Optimize recommendations

Action items (brief): see action_items field for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we got most folks, um i'll kick off — i'm samira from redwood, our team today is diego and aisha, we'll run through a quick hosted api demo focusing on embeddings and our rerank endpoint, and then dig into any integration questions.
[00:35] Marta: thanks samira, excited, quick context — we're Spectral Insights, we power semantic search over large media transcripts and docs, our current infra uses a vector DB and some homegrown reranker but relevance drifts as new content arrives, so looking for a more stable hosted path.
[01:12] Diego: perfect, that's exactly the pattern we see. quick question on qps and latency — what's the typical query volume and acceptable p95 latency for results?
[01:28] Jonah: right now proto is 120 rps bursts up to 800 during morning ingest, tail latency target is p95 under 350ms for search results, but we can accept 600ms for heavier rerank steps if it improves quality.
[01:50] Aisha: okay cool. just to set expectations, hosted api can give you lower ops overhead and fast ramp, but if you need consistent p95 under 150ms and guaranteed throughput you might look at dedicated capacity. we'll show how hosted can be tuned first.
[02:12] Ethan: and security — we have to be SOC2 compliant and we need SSO + audit logs, also curious about KMS options for keys.
[02:24] Samira: yes, we'll cover that, we have SOC2 docs, SAML SSO integrations, and KMS/HSM support for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations though — we'll attach the security brief after the call.
[02:49] Diego: ok jumping into the demo. i'll share my screen — starting with embeddings endpoint. typical flow: ingest docs -> compute embeddings -> store in your vector DB (you mentioned Pinecone right?) -> at query time generate query embedding -> candidate retrieval -> rerank via our rerank endpoint that scores full context.
[03:20] Jonah: yep we use an in-memory index now and experimented with pinecone for prod. how does the reranker differ from doing the scoring client-side?
[03:33] Diego: good question. the rerank endpoint accepts a set of candidate doc ids plus their context or embeddings, and returns a score and optional structured output. the key difference is you can send full context and let our hosted model do cross-attention reranking which often improves MRR without you doing heavy modeling. also we support streaming tokens if you want explainability output.
[03:59] Marta: any limits on candidate size? we usually pull top-200 candidates initially.
[04:07] Aisha: supported size today is flexible but practical sweet spot is 50-200 for latency/cost tradeoffs. for extreme scale we recommend a two-stage cascade: small candidate set for fast paths, then rerank top N.
[04:29] Jonah: ok that matches our thinking. can you show the console traces for a sample rerank call?
[04:36] Diego: switching over — here's the console, per-request traces show token-level timing, model variant, cache hits for prefix caching, and cost breakdown tokens in/out. you can also see suggested batching settings in the Optimize tab based on observed request patterns.
[05:05] Samira: note the Optimize recommendation flagged that for mostly short queries batching 16 with a max latency SLO of 300ms gives best cost reductions — that is a suggestion, you can tune.
[05:22] Ethan: when you say cache hits, what exactly is cached? can we cache KV from prefix prompts?
[05:29] Diego: yes, we do prefix and KV caching for stateful chat flows and repeated prompt prefixes. for rerank we cache static document prefixes you send as part of context, reducing per-token compute. caching behavior is visible in traces.
[05:50] Marta: curious about models — are these open models or proprietary? we prefer open models for reproducibility.
[05:57] Aisha: we host a catalog of open models with performance profiles and also verified variants that are optimized for latency/cost. for reranking we often recommend a specific quantized open checkpoint but if you have stronger quality needs we can run an eval against your test set.
[06:20] Jonah: evals — do you support running our test suite within your platform?
[06:26] Diego: yes, we can ingest prompt sets and SFT-like evals; Optimize can surface regressions and suggest model switching. we'd ask you to share a labeled set and we'll run a baseline.
[06:42] Samira: let's demo a live request — i'll run a query through the embeddings endpoint -> retrieval -> rerank. you'll see candidate generation done client-side (we'll simulate via the console) and a rerank call.
[07:01] Diego: running now... [07:08] (sound of typing) ...response in 420ms, score distribution shows top-3 distinct confidence, and we returned a structured answer with explanation tokens.
[07:20] Priya: that 420ms is for the rerank call only?
[07:24] Diego: yes, that's rerank only. end-to-end including retrieval is additive. with our recommended batching and candidate sizing you can often keep end-to-end under 350-450ms for moderate sets.
[07:40] Jonah: what's cost like for these rerank calls compared to doing token scoring client-side?
[07:47] Aisha: rerank is more expensive per request since it runs cross-attention, but it reduces engineering time and often improves quality so less manual tuning. Optimize can estimate your per-call token cost and project monthly spend given qps.
[08:05] Marta: okay, question on data retention and logs — do you keep transcripts or do you redact? we need to ensure PII isn't stored.
[08:15] Samira: you can set data retention policies per project. hosted keeps short retention by default but we can set zero retention for sensitive workloads; for enterprise deployments we support private control plane and on-prem where no customer data leaves the VPC.
[08:35] Ethan: for compliance we'd want audit logs for every model invocation and per-token cost attribution for billing. is that available?
[08:44] Diego: yes, Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-request metadata (caller id, route, model). Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[09:02] Jonah: our main concern is throughput during peak. can hosted scale to 800 rps?
[09:10] Aisha: hosted can burst, but predictability at that scale is best with Dedicated. we often recommend starting hosted for POC then moving to Dedicated reserved capacity once SLA is required. we can also route critical traffic to dedicated pool while keeping other traffic on hosted to save cost.
[09:32] Marta: can we pin model versions during rollouts to avoid regressions?
[09:35] Diego: yes, you can pin model versions and use canary rollouts. Console supports A/B and automatic fallback to previous variant on regressions.
[09:48] Priya: curious about integration patterns — our retrieval currently returns doc ids and small text snippets. how do you recommend calling rerank?
[09:58] Diego: common pattern: step1 generate embeddings for docs and queries, step2 retrieve top K embeddings from vector DB, step3 call rerank with the full snippet or concatenated context for top N (say 50), step4 present top results. alternatively you can send only embeddings into rerank if you want faster calls but quality can drop.
[10:25] Jonah: do you support binary payloads for embeddings to reduce transfer?
[10:30] Aisha: we support efficient protobuf payloads via SDKs; REST accepts json but sdk can be more compact.
[10:40] Samira: small note — some customers use a hybrid approach: approximate nearest neighbor to a small candidate set then rerank with full context. that'll be lower cost than reranking 200 each time.
[10:56] Ethan: another security note — are model footprints ever logged in a way that could leak prompts?
[11:02] Diego: by default we log meta info not raw prompts; you can opt out of logging raw inputs or have zero retention. enterprise can go private so prompts never leave your network.
[11:18] Marta: okay, i'd like to see example payloads for the rerank endpoint — both embeddings-in and context-in.
[11:25] Diego: sure, i'll paste examples into the meeting chat post-call, but here's a quick pseudo: {endpoint: /v1/rerank, body: {query: ..., candidates: [{id: 123, text: "..."}, ...]}} — response is scores array with optional explain tokens.
[11:53] Jonah: do you provide SDKs in python and js?
[11:56] Aisha: yes python, js, and go community libs, plus example notebooks for embeddings->indexing->rerank. we'll share the notebook as part of the follow-up.
[12:10] Samira: switching to Optimize tab real quick — this is where we synthesize telemetry and suggest tuning: batch sizes, quantization profiles, and model switches. see this baseline recommendation for your query profile.
[12:28] Marta: what's the quantization suggestion? we worry about quality drop with int8.
[12:33] Diego: Optimize suggests int8 for most candidate generation models where small quality delta is acceptable, and leaves a higher-precision variant for rerank. you can test on your eval set to measure MRR drop.
[12:49] Priya: can Optimize run differential tests automatically? like, if we switch to a quantized variant it runs A/B and reports deltas?
[12:56] Aisha: yes, we can run evaluation sweeps and surface significant regressions tied to prompt sets. we also integrate with your internal test harness if you provide it.
[13:10] Jonah: let's talk about an actual POC: what would success metrics look like?
[13:15] Samira: typical POC success: measurable increase in MRR or NDCG on your labeled set, end-to-end p95 within agreed SLO, and cost per query within agreed threshold. we usually propose a 4-week POC with a labeled test set.
[13:33] Ethan: timeline — we want something by end of q1. is that realistic?
[13:37] Diego: yes if we get sample data and your eval set this week we can spin up a pilot and run baseline comparisons within 2-3 weeks.
[13:49] Marta: stakeholder question: finance will need monthly cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated.
[13:55] Samira: we'll prepare a side-by-side including amortized reserved costs for dedicated.
[14:05] Priya: any known limitations with long documents? we deal with long media transcripts sometimes 50k tokens.
[14:13] Aisha: for very long docs we recommend segmenting and indexing segments with metadata; rerank can accept concatenated top segments but watch token budgets. we also support chunked retrieval and synthetic summarization to reduce context length.
[14:34] Jonah: are there any pre-built rerank prompts or recipes?
[14:38] Diego: yes we have prompt library and rerank templates in the Console examples — you can adapt them.
[14:47] Marta: you mentioned fallback policies earlier — can you explain?
[14:52] Samira: fallback policies route to compatible model variants based on region, capacity, or cost tier. e.g., if low-latency pool is saturated we route to mid-latency variant with similar quality.
[15:03] Ethan: what about on-prem or VPC? we may need this for compliance.
[15:09] Samira: Private deployment options include VPC with private control plane and an on-prem bundle for air-gapped environments. those come with licensing and support contracts.
[15:20] Jonah: what's the ramp cost for private?
[15:23] Samira: it's an enterprise engagement — we'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[15:34] Diego: back to the demo — i want to show a trace where Optimize suggested reducing batch size because tail latency spiked due to token distribution. see this request where most queries are short but some have very long contexts; Optimize highlighted a misconfiguration.
[15:54] Priya: interesting. can Optimize automatically set autoscale rules?
[15:58] Aisha: it suggests autoscale policy thresholds but we leave final policies to you; for Dedicated we can also implement custom autoscalers.
[16:12] Marta: okay can we talk about data residency? some of our customers in EU require data to stay in EU.
[16:18] Samira: we have regional hosting in eu-west and can route traffic to eu-only clusters; for strict residency the private deployment is recommended.
[16:29] Jonah: competitor question — how does Redwood compare to Pinecone plus OpenAI rerank?
[16:35] Diego: Pinecone handles vector indexing well but you'd still call OpenAI for rerank and manage orchestration. Redwood bundles the serving runtime, rerank, routing, and observability in one platform optimized for production costs and latency with built-in offline evals — so less glue code.
[16:55] Marta: does Redwood host Pinecone as a partner or do we need to manage vector DB separately?
[17:01] Aisha: you can use any vector store; we integrate with common ones. some customers use our recommended embedded stores for convenience.
[17:12] Jonah: logging question — is there a per-token cost attribution for each route for finance?
[17:17] Samira: yes that's baked into the Console cost reports.
[17:27] Ethan: okay let's surface some concrete POC scope items now.
[17:31] Priya: we'll provide a 10k doc subset + labeled queries, expected qps profile and our current candidate size.
[17:38] Marta: success metric: +12% NDCG on our dev set and end-to-end p95 < 450ms.
[17:46] Samira: got it. Diego, can you run the baseline and propose model/config?
[17:51] Diego: yes i'll run baseline once we get data. i'm thinking a two-stage pipeline: embedding candidate retrieval with a compact model + rerank with a higher-precision open model. we'll test quantized variants.
[18:06] Jonah: sounds good. what about SLA for hosted during the POC?
[18:11] Samira: POC is not SLA-backed but we provide priority support. Dedicated comes with SLA.
[18:20] Ethan: one more question: can rerank outputs be deterministic? we need reproducible scoring.
[18:26] Diego: yes if you pin model and set deterministic sampling parameters the rerank can be deterministic; however, some model variants have nondeterminism in GPU kernels, but we can meet reproducibility requirements through pinned variants and controlled runtimes.
[18:45] Priya: ok let's talk pricing — ballpark hosted per-embedding + rerank token cost?
[18:51] Samira: ballpark numbers in the pricing sheet we'll send; rerank is higher since it uses cross-attention, embedding costs are lower. we'll send specific per-token estimates for your qps in the follow-up.
[19:06] Marta: i'd like an example of an end-to-end cost calc for 200k queries/day with avg candidate size 50.
[19:13] Samira: noted, we'll run that and include in follow-up.
[19:20] Diego: also note you can use prefilling and caching to lower cost for repeated queries.
[19:29] Jonah: anything else on the demo?
[19:32] Diego: one more thing — if you want explainability we can return highlight spans and token-level attributions in rerank response. that increased token output but helps product teams.
[19:45] Marta: that's useful.
[19:48] Samira: at this point i'd like to recap next steps. we'll: 1) send security brief and SOC2/SSO/KMS docs (Samira) 2) share sample notebook + rerank payloads (Diego) 3) Spectral to share labeled subset and qps profile (Jonah/Priya) 4) schedule POC kickoff (all) — target date 2026-01-21.
[20:15] Jonah: timeline works, we'll aim to share data by 2026-01-14.
[20:21] Ethan: finance will need the hosted vs dedicated cost sheet, include reserved pricing.
[20:27] Samira: will do. last quick question — who is the account executive for this?
[20:31] Samira: that's me, i'm your AE, diego and aisha will be SE support.
[20:37] Marta: great thanks everyone.
[20:40] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[20:45] (meeting wraps, small chatter)

Note: transcript truncated but representative; timestamps approximate and transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and filler words as typical of automated meeting transcription.
